original_value: Human trajectory prediction is an essential task for various applications such as travel recommendation, location-sensitive advertisement, and traffic planning. Most existing approaches are sequential-model based and produce a prediction by mining behavior patterns. However, the effectiveness of pattern-based methods is not as good as expected in real-life conditions, such as data sparse or data missing. Moreover, due to the technical limitations of sensors or the traffic situation at the given time, people going to the same place may produce different trajectories. Even for people traveling along the same route, the observed transit records are not exactly the same. Therefore trajectories are always diverse, and extracting user intention from trajectories is difficult. In this paper, we propose an augmented-intention recurrent neural network (AI-RNN) model to predict locations in diverse trajectories. We first propose three strategies to generate graph structures to demonstrate travel context and then leverage graph convolutional networks to augment user travel intentions under graph view. Finally, we use gated recurrent units with augmented node vectors to predict human trajectories. We experiment with two representative real-life datasets and evaluate the performance of the proposed model by comparing its results with those of other state-of-the-art models. The results demonstrate that the AI-RNN model outperforms other methods in terms of top-k accuracy, especially in scenarios with low similarity.

result.paraphrase: Human trajectory prediction is a key task for applications including travel recommendation, location-aware advertising, and traffic planning. Most existing methods rely on sequential models and make predictions by learning behavior patterns. In real-world settings, however, pattern-based approaches are less effective than expected when data are sparse or missing. In addition, because of sensor limitations or the traffic conditions at a given time, people heading to the same destination may generate different trajectories. Even when traveling the same route, the observed transit records are not identical. As a result, trajectories are highly diverse, making it difficult to infer user intention from them. In this paper, we present an augmented-intention recurrent neural network (AI-RNN) model for predicting locations in diverse trajectories. We first design three strategies to generate graph structures that capture travel context, then use graph convolutional networks to augment user travel intentions from the graph perspective. Finally, we apply gated recurrent units with augmented node vectors to predict human trajectories. We evaluate the proposed model on two representative real-world datasets and compare it with other state-of-the-art methods. The results show that AI-RNN achieves better top-k accuracy than other approaches, especially in low-similarity scenarios.
